task.description: Perform WF-02 Step 1b (design gate, hard gate) for REQ-386 per docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md. Read lib/letflow/design/req386-attachment-signed-links.md independently and in full. For each of the six acceptance criteria, verify: a corresponding concrete design element exists (no TBD/deferral language); function signatures are fully specified including error shape; cross-module dependencies are listed and complete; no implementation code is present. Give particular scrutiny to the INV-5/AC4 byte-identical-response mechanical argument -- trace verify/3's control flow, the router handler's branching, and the response helper's argument surface directly against the design text. Verify the 300s expiry is stated with rationale and flagged as a REVIEWER judgment call. Verify the no-migration-needed claim against the actual lib/letflow/secrets.ex source. Confirm no scope creep beyond REQ-386.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: authenticated :AttachmentsRead-scoped endpoint issues a signed link with a stated, bounded expiry
AC2: same link refused after expiry with plain-language message, no bytes returned, test-injectable clock
AC3: fresh link after a prior expired one succeeds and serves the document normally
AC4: expired-or-invalid response byte-identical for cross-tenant vs. never-issued attachment id
AC5: fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 and its existing tests are unchanged
AC6: mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test both pass; SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off required before merge

result.summary: Read lib/letflow/design/req386-attachment-signed-links.md in full, independently, plus lib/letflow/secrets.ex (full) and the live lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex to check the design's factual claims against shipped code. All six acceptance criteria map to concrete design elements with no TBD/deferral language (traceability table in the design's own §0). issue/3, verify/3, both new route handlers (handle_issue_attachment_link/3, handle_get_attachment_link_content/3), the private helpers (get_or_create_signing_key_id/2, unpinned_reference/1, pinned_reference/2, link_content_url/3, verify_link_token/2, check_attachment_id_matches/2), the new Error.attachment_link_expired/0 and Response.attachment_link_expired/1 pair, and the two new Authorization.endpoint_policy_key/2 clauses all carry full @spec-style signatures with explicit {:ok,_}/{:error,_} tagged unions -- no implicit error shape anywhere. Cross-module dependency table in §8 checked against every module actually referenced in the document body (Letflow.Secrets, Letflow.Identity, Letflow.Repository.Attachments (indirect), Letflow.Routers.Instances, Letflow.Api.Response/Error, Letflow.Api.Authorization, Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter, Letflow.Api.Context, plus Jason/:crypto/Base for the new module) -- complete, nothing referenced in body text is missing from the table. Scanned the whole file for implementation code: every code block is either a bare @spec/@type, a route-macro declaration whose body is a one-line delegation to a named handler, or a trivial one-line function clause (endpoint_policy_key/2 clauses, Response.attachment_link_expired/1's single-expression body) -- calibrated directly against lib/letflow/design/req212-instance-attachments-routes.md (a prior PASSING design for the same router), which contains the identical class of literal one-line endpoint_policy_key/2 clauses and route declarations (§6.3) and was accepted; no def...do...end block with real branching/business logic is present anywhere in this document. Traced the INV-5/AC4 mechanical argument directly against the design text: verify/3's six failure-causing steps (malformed token shape, JSON decode/shape failure, unknown requester tenant, Secrets.resolve/2 failure on the pinned per-tenant key -- confirmed its documented error-atom set {:not_found, :tenant_mismatch, :disabled, :deleted, :invalid_reference, :purpose_not_allowed} matches lib/letflow/secrets.ex's actual @spec for resolve/2 verbatim -- signature mismatch via :crypto.hash_equals/2, and expiry) all funnel into one shared `with/else` clause returning the single value {:error, :expired_or_invalid}, with no computation between a failure branch and that return that could vary the value. The router's own with-chain (§3.2 step 3) calls verify_link_token/2 strictly before check_attachment_id_matches/2 and before fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3, so no attachment-identity-dependent code executes on any verification-failure path; check_attachment_id_matches/2's own mismatch case also folds into {:error, :expired_or_invalid} rather than :not_found, keeping exactly one failure class. Response.attachment_link_expired/1 takes only `conn` -- no caller-suppliable argument that could vary status/headers/body. Confirmed the cross-tenant mechanism is genuinely structural, not conventional: because the signing key is per-tenant and verify/3 always resolves the secret under the REQUESTER's own tenant_id (never a tenant decoded from the token, since the token carries no tenant field at all), a token issued by tenant A and presented by tenant B either finds no secret at all for tenant B (not_found) or a real-but-different key (signature mismatch) -- both collapse to the same value before AttachmentLinks.verify/3 returns, so the router literally cannot distinguish it from a fabricated/never-issued token. Verified route placement and existing helper reuse directly against the live lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex: fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 (line 1159) and fetch_scoped_attachment_metadata/3 (line 1186) exist exactly as the design describes them and are not modified by this design; authz_delete '/:id/attachments/:attachment_id' (line 390) and authz_get '/:id' (line 394) confirm the design's stated route-ordering placement is correct. The 300s expiry (§2.1) is stated explicitly with rationale (short enough to devalue a leaked/logged URL, long enough for a slow-connection document load) and is explicitly flagged for REVIEWER as a judgment call, same precedent class as REQ-211's own @max_upload_bytes -- not silently decided. The no-migration-needed claim (§6) was checked against the actual lib/letflow/secrets.ex source, not just the design's account of it: check_purpose_allowed(:generic, :generic) -> :ok exists verbatim in the shipped module (line 334), confirming purpose: :generic / consumer: :generic is already a legal pair and no change to Letflow.Secrets is needed. No scope creep found: fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 itself is explicitly stated unchanged and reused verbatim (confirmed against the live file); REQ-387's frontend viewer and REQ-388's audit logging are explicitly named as out of scope and not touched anywhere in the document. OQ-1 (auth pipeline placement), OQ-2 (token versioning), and OQ-3 (response body key names) are genuine open questions flagged for REVIEWER, not silent resolutions of anything an acceptance criterion requires -- none of them leaves an acceptance criterion itself unaddressed.
